title: A Comprehensive Survey of Bias in LLMs: Current Landscape and Future Directions
measurement_description: This paper is a comprehensive survey reviewing existing literature on bias in Large Language Models. While it covers various forms of bias (gender, racial, age, socioeconomic), it specifically reviews methods for mitigating religious biases. It references the 'Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)' framework, which aims to mitigate gender, racial, and religious biases in LLM-generated English text. It also discusses 'Social Contact Debiasing (SCD)', which measures 13 types of social bias (implied to potentially include religion given the context of social biases) in models like LLaMA 2.
findings: The survey highlights that religious bias is a recognized category of social bias in LLMs, alongside gender and racial bias. It notes that techniques like Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) have been shown to effectively reduce religious biases in generated text by favoring less biased completions. Additionally, the Social Contact Debiasing (SCD) technique was found to reduce social biases (a category containing religious bias) in LLaMA 2 by up to 40% after one epoch of tuning.
